final_text:
## Incident Report: 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence:** `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 packets, 26 MB, capture spans 2026-01-27 23:04:03 to 23:14:27 UTC, ~624s). No accompanying IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived entirely from packet-level analysis with tshark.

### Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.1.21.58 |
| MAC address | 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-ES9F3ML |
| AD domain | WIN11OFFICE.COM (DC: WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com, 10.1.21.2) |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos AS/TGS exchange between 10.1.21.58 and the DC, realm WIN11OFFICE.COM) |

Confirmed via DHCP Discover/Request (option 12 hostname + option 81 client FQDN `DESKTOP-ES9F3ML.win11office.com`) and NBNS name registrations for both DESKTOP-ES9F3ML and the domain WIN11OFFICE.

### Malware family and attribution

**Behavioral attribution only — not signature-confirmed.** No AV/YARA/Suricata detections were provided, and the payload itself was delivered over TLS (Cloudflare, with ECH masking SNI as `cloudflare-ech.com`), so no binary was recovered from the capture for static/hash-based confirmation.

Based on network behavior, this matches the profile of a commodity **information-stealer distributed via a fake file-download portal**, consistent with the **Lumma Stealer (LummaC2)** delivery/C2 pattern:
- A JS-based browser fingerprinting gate (canvas, WebGL, AudioContext, fonts, hardware, screen) served from the C2 before/after infection.
- A REST-style check-in endpoint (`/api/set_agent`) using an `id`/`token` bot identifier and an `act=log` exfil call, cycling through each installed browser (Chrome, then Edge).
- Victim data staged server-side as a per-victim archive named `<public-ip>-<hash>.zip`.
- Delivery via disposable, typo-squat-style "file hosting" domains on abused TLDs (`.lat`, `.sbs`, `.cyou`, `.cc`).

This is the strongest behavioral match available; it should be treated as a working hypothesis pending sample/AV confirmation, not a confirmed classification.

### Infection timeline (all times relative to capture start)

| t (s) | Domain | Resolved IP | Activity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45.3 | hiyter.com | 104.21.22.231 | Initial lure/landing page |
| 45.8 | media.megafilehub4.lat | 104.21.48.156 | Fake file-hosting intermediate page (217 KB) |
| 48.3–70.7 | arch.filemegahab4.sbs | 104.21.46.67:443 | **Payload download** — 16 MB fetched over TLS (Chrome JA3 `09cc8725fe30ac191df5cf6b3365f528`, ECH-masked SNI `cloudflare-ech.com`) |
| 90.3 | whooptm.cyou | 62.72.32.156:443 | Post-execution check-in |
| 92.3–103.0 | **whitepepper.su** | **153.92.1.49:80 (plaintext HTTP)** | **C2 check-in** — repeated GET/POST to `/api/set_agent`, browser fingerprint exfil |
| 122.8 | holiday-forever.cc | 80.97.160.24:443 | Secondary C2/redirector contact |
| 126.5–132.1 | communicationfirewall-security.cc | 104.21.9.36:443 | Secondary C2/redirector contact |

No further malicious traffic occurs after t≈132s; the remaining ~490s of capture is normal Windows/AD background noise (LDAP, Kerberos, SMB2/SAMR/LSARPC to the DC, Microsoft/Google/MSN telemetry).

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / malicious endpoints (IP:port):**
- 153.92.1.49:80 — whitepepper.su (primary C2, plaintext HTTP)
- 104.21.46.67:443 — arch.filemegahab4.sbs (payload host)
- 104.21.48.156:443 — media.megafilehub4.lat
- 104.21.22.231:443 — hiyter.com
- 62.72.32.156:443 — whooptm.cyou
- 80.97.160.24:443 — holiday-forever.cc
- 104.21.9.36:443 — communicationfirewall-security.cc

**Malicious domains:**
- whitepepper.su
- arch.filemegahab4.sbs
- media.megafilehub4.lat
- hiyter.com
- whooptm.cyou
- holiday-forever.cc
- communicationfirewall-security.cc

**Malicious URL (C2 API, observed as both GET and POST):**
```
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome[&act=log]
http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?...&agent=Edge&act=log
```
Bot ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C` / Token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

**Referenced artifact (named by the C2 in its response body, not a file directly captured in the pcap):**
- `172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip` — the C2 returned `cant open archive 172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1.zip` in response to the `act=log` POST. `038485b1855ec7a1ba5bbda042ad17a1` is a 32-character (MD5-length) hash, not SHA256, and `172.56.88.98` is consistent with the victim's carrier-NAT public IP — indicating a per-victim exfil archive naming scheme, not a hash we independently computed.

**No SHA256 hash of the actual malware payload could be obtained.** The 16 MB payload delivered from arch.filemegahab4.sbs was transferred entirely inside TLS with Cloudflare ECH; no plaintext executable (no MZ/PE header) was observed anywhere in the capture, so its hash cannot be derived from this pcap alone.
